name: Skip Link
summary: A skip link is the first focusable thing in the document, and the shortest route past everything a keyboard user would otherwise Tab through. Use it to satisfy SC 2.4.1. It is clipped rather than hidden, because the three usual ways of hiding something also make it unfocusable.
demoNote: No JavaScript on this page. Click inside a frame and press Shift+Tab to reach its link. The two failures in Common mistakes are live, so you can Tab through them and watch.

contract.useWhen: The first focusable thing on the page, and a target that accepts focus.
keyboard: it has to be the first stop — nothing focusable may precede it
follows it; the ring on the target is the only confirmation of the jump
failureModes: display:none to hide it, which makes it unfocusable — the most common broken skip link there is
:focus-visible instead of :focus, so a programmatic focus leaves it invisible
no tabindex=-1 on the target, so the page scrolls and the next Tab resumes at the top
a border in the clipped state, which border-box cannot shrink below: a 1px box becomes 4px
no white-space:nowrap, so the text wraps inside 1px and is read a letter at a time
a cookie banner focusable before it
